curriculum.lesson_evidence: Throwing and catching games turn skills into play with rules, scoring and teamwork. Good games use soft balls, clear space and rules such as throwing below shoulder height and never at someone's head. Fair games give everyone turns and can be adjusted, for example with a larger or lighter ball, a shorter distance or a seated option, so all players can join in. The goal is to take part and improve, not to show off.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
A game has a rule that only the best catchers get the ball. Rewrite the rule so the game is fair and say why.

FEEDBACK
Rewrite: 'Everyone must receive the ball once before anyone receives it twice.' Fair play means every player has turns, so everyone can improve and feels included.

WATCH FOR
Believing games are only fun if you win. Fun comes from taking part, improving and playing fairly; scores are for the game, not for judging people.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Invent a throwing and catching game for three players using a soft ball and a target. Write the rules, the scoring, two safety rules and two ways to adjust the game for different abilities. Play two rounds and record how well the rules worked.

Write a short reflection naming one choice you changed and why. Any movement is optional, adult-supervised and can be done in a gentler way or described instead.

teaching.why: This helps the learner make safe, healthy and respectful choices using clear cues and reasons, rather than guessing or copying others. Every choice keeps bodies safe and includes everyone.

teaching.feedback: The new situation should use the same PDHPE idea as the example, but happen in a different place or with different people.
teaching.fix: Change the choice or strategy, not just the wording.
teaching.guided_attempt: Describe or practise one fresh situation that uses the same skill and write a short reason for your choice.
teaching.misconception: Repeating the worked example cannot show transfer to a new situation.
teaching.model: Throwing and catching games turn skills into play with rules, scoring and teamwork. Good games use soft balls, clear space and rules such as throwing below shoulder height and never at someone's head. Fair games give everyone turns and can be adjusted, for example with a larger or lighter ball, a shorter distance or a seated option, so all players can join in. The goal is to take part and improve, not to show off. Now choose a different situation to show you can transfer the idea.
teaching.rule: Use the same PDHPE idea in a new place, game or situation, not a copy of the example. Review safety, fairness and inclusion.
